published_statement: NOT QUOTED -- the source was not read. What follows is the standard gloss, from memory, and MUST NOT be treated as a quotation: Penrose (1979) proposed that the Weyl curvature is constrained to vanish (or be small) at initial singularities while unconstrained at final ones, as the geometric origin of the thermodynamic arrow of time, and heuristically associated Weyl curvature with gravitational entropy. The tree's version (READ): 'The early universe was in a state of extremely low GRAVITATIONAL entropy -- Weyl curvature near zero, Penrose's hypothesis -- and gravitational clumping raises it. Structure formation is genuinely a relaxation' (permute.py:87-91).
published_hypotheses: NOT READ at source; listed as the tree records them and as the standard gloss (unverified):
H1 (tree, canonical entry) gravitational entropy exists and is measured by Weyl curvature -- a conjecture; no general definition is accepted (literature claim, not READ here).
H3 (gloss, unverified) the constraint applies at INITIAL singularities (past-type), not at final ones -- the time-asymmetry is imposed as a boundary condition, not derived.
H4 (gloss, unverified) the hypothesis is a conjecture about the universe's initial state, offered to explain the second law; it is not a theorem of GR.
hypothesis_drift: STATUS DROPPED inside the tree (READ): permute.py:88-89 names it 'Penrose's hypothesis', but permute.py:441-443 prints 'Penrose: the early universe had near-zero Weyl curvature, so gravitational clumping IS a relaxation' and permute.py:543-545 prints 'the early universe had near-zero Weyl curvature and gravitational clumping raises entropy, so STRUCTURE FORMATION genuinely is a relaxation' -- the conjecture is stated as fact in the verdict text.

DECLARED, NOT COMPUTED (READ): permute.py:273 hardcodes RELAXATION_BELONGS_TO = 'the rearrangement' and permute.py:439-440 checks it against the same literal -- the chk is tautological; the scorecard row 'it is a structural relaxation / SPLIT / the REARRANGEMENT relaxes' (permute.py:507-508) rests on this literal plus the named hypothesis, while its other half (isentropic expansion, permute.py:434-437) IS computed.

H1 WEAKENED to 'measured by Weyl curvature' (permute.py:88-89) without naming a measure: computed here (C2) that C_abcd C^abcd = 48M^2/r^6 in a Ricci-flat Schwarzschild exterior and is identical for the time-reversed (white-hole) geometry, so a Weyl scalar carries no arrow by itself; any Weyl-entropy reading needs a chosen measure and the past-singularity boundary condition (H3). The tree names neither.

ADDED (permute.py:90-91, 544-546): 'relaxation' == increase of gravitational entropy. The WCH (as glossed, unverified) constrains the initial state; 'relaxation' is the tree's own term, supplied by it, not by the source.

SCOPE (unverified against source): tree says 'the early universe' (permute.py:88, 441, 543); the standard gloss restricts the constraint to the initial singularity. Not asserted as a drift until read.

H2 REGIME DROPPED (permute.py:89-90, 544-545): 'clumping raises it' is computed here (C3) only for the linear, sub-horizon Einstein-de Sitter regime and only for Weyl/Ricci and Hubble-normalised Weyl-electric ratios, where it reduces to Poisson's equation (|E|/rho = delta/sqrt(6) in both modes). The tree states it without regime or measure.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/penrose-weyl-curvature-hypothesis.out). C1: FLRW k=0,+1,-1 -- all 256 Weyl components vanish identically (conformally flat), so 'Weyl near zero' == 'near FLRW'. C2: Schwarzschild R_ab = 0 and C_abcd C^abcd = Kretschmann = 48M^2/r^6; same scalar for the white-hole time-reverse -- no arrow from the scalar alone. C3: linear sub-horizon EdS dust, growing (Phi const, delta ~ a) and decaying (Phi ~ a^-5/2, delta ~ a^-3/2) modes: |E|/rho = delta/sqrt(6) exactly in both, and |E|/H^2 rises iff delta rises -- 'clumping raises the Weyl measure' holds in this regime for these measures, and is Poisson's equation. C4: virial E = -K gives C = dE/dT = -3Nk_B/2 < 0 (negative heat capacity; the standard thermodynamic reason clumped states are favoured under gravity -- a kinetic-entropy argument, not a Weyl one). C5: S_BH ~ 10^122.9 (1e80 baryons) vs 10^122.8 (Planck 2018) vs S_rad ~ 10^90; gap > 30 dex under both. What is NOT checkable here: that any Weyl-based quantity IS an entropy (no accepted definition; a conjecture, not a finite claim), and the nonlinear (virialised, black-hole) regime.

lacked_data: What Penrose (1979) lacked: the detection of primordial CMB anisotropy (~1e-5, COBE 1992 onward) and precision cosmological parameters. Evidence either way, computed here: (a) the modern baryon count (Planck 2018, READ via sibling audit) moves the gravitational-maximum exponent by -0.09 dex (10^122.9 -> 10^122.8) and leaves a >30 dex gap to the radiation entropy (C5) -- the 'extremely low entropy' conclusion does not move; (b) the later smoothness data support the geometric half (near-FLRW, and FLRW has C_abcd == 0 exactly, C1); (c) neither datum bears on the ENTROPY interpretation, which is a missing DEFINITION, not missing data -- no measurement since 1979 decides whether Weyl curvature measures entropy. So M's hypothesis is not supported for this result on present evidence: the part that depends on data is unmoved; the part that is uncertain is uncertain for conceptual, not observational, reasons.
grade_evidence: The source could not be read in this stage: Penrose 1979 is pre-arXiv and its intended restatement (arXiv:1303.5612) was unreachable -- alphaXiv returned 'quota exceeded' on all four calls, and arXiv plus every mirror is egress-blocked (403, not retried). Under M's rules an unread source is OPEN, never flattened. What WAS established, and would carry into a graded audit: (1) computed -- FLRW is exactly conformally flat (C1), so the observational half ('early universe near-zero Weyl') is equivalent to near-homogeneity and is not contradicted by any datum used; (2) computed -- 'clumping raises it' holds for Weyl/Ricci and Hubble-normalised Weyl-electric ratios in linear EdS in both modes (C3), but Weyl scalars carry no arrow by themselves (C2) and no finite check decides that any Weyl quantity IS an entropy; (3) READ in the tree -- permute.py drops the hypothesis status at 441-443 and 543-547 and the scorecard's 'REARRANGEMENT relaxes' half rests on a hardcoded literal checked against itself (273, 439-440). Once the source is read, the expected grade is NARROWED (regime and measure dropped, conjecture printed as fact), not WRONG: nothing here refutes the hypothesis, and nothing here upgrades it from conjecture.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: reading Penrose's statement via an arXiv restatement (1303.5612 sec. 1, or a WCH review) confirming (i) it is a conjecture on initial singularities, (ii) no accepted definition of gravitational entropy -- then the tree's unqualified use at permute.py:441-443, 543-547 and the literal at 273 are narrowing drifts. To STANDS: the tree carrying 'Penrose's conjecture' at every use and computing, not hardcoding, RELAXATION_BELONGS_TO for a named measure in a named regime (C3 shows this is possible in linear theory), with the source read and agreeing. To WRONG: a READ counterexample (e.g. 2004.10222, Bonnor) showing a Weyl measure DEcreasing under clumping in the regime the tree uses, reproduced here -- a measure-dependent failure would narrow, not refute. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a datum that moves the >30 dex entropy gap, which C5 shows none has.
